newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 2.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Government's labor law revision bill calls for utilizing substitute workers in a workplace to replace workers on strike: government's draft revision bill to be finalised tomorrow, and to be submitted to the National Assembly December 10.

- Seoul-Pusan rail operation suspended for about an hour on Sunday night as about 21cm of rail ripped apart at point 61 km from Seoul for unknown reasons, but apparently as a result of fatigue factor coupled with impact of sudden cold.

- North Korea-U.S. negotiation on opening liaison office concluded, but opening timing left to be decided depending on pyongyang's circumstance: japan's mainich shimbun quoting a diplomatic source in Seoul.

- Government party is able to win presidential election against whoever opposition candidate, Kim Dae-jung or Kim Jong-pil, is pitted against : ruling party chairman, Lee Hong-koo, says in an interview with Chosun Ilbo.
- Korean marathoner Lee, atlanta olympic silver medalist, wins fukuoka international marathon event on Sunday.
- Korean prosecutors issue order to crack down of swindlers involved in some 600 cases of cons perpetrated against China-Based ethnic Koreans seeking jobs in Korea.
- Mercury plunges to minus 7 degrees C in Seoul early today.
- U.S. commerce secretary Kantor says progress made with China on trade, human rights issue.
